paragraphs.llm_text: Wednesday 24th wind west cloudy with a gale of wind throughout the day. Men employed there, two in the tannery house three working at Thee, blacksmith in the forge making Nails &c. Dunning making a window for Provision Shed, Adam & George mending the Roof of Lake House, three Boys sent to Mussquito point with Nets Mr Dunning set two at Buckholds point. James Dunning, his sons came here last evening & brought 3 Lake white Fish & 35 Jack Suchers, that they got out of one net at Churchill creek in two days, he also killed 2 Geese & 10 Ducks which is always so much in this scarce time.

lines.transcription: Monday 29th Wind variable & light, men employed thus James
Running 2 two men out whalling both tides & Killed one whale & B.r-
home the one from Stage that Buck Killed on the 26th. Buck was
on the stage this day tide but got no chance the winter, or tide is
very low now. William Oman visited the nets at Cerekotos point &
Wmly caught 2 small Salmon out of six Nets, he then with his
son and Andrew Dunning went across with the whalving & Tent
set some Nett, there also, three men working at Provisions I had
Adam & Geys son piling up boards. Ther: 7 7 above zero.

lines.transcription: Sunday 12th Wind west of changed to N W. blew a gale
in the forenoon, two Chipewgans arrived from Inland, they will
be traded with tomorrow, 1 Salmon & 13 River which fish from the
Petr across & at Quickolds. point. no fish from nets at the
back of the Rocks. W. Oman brought the nets home to
day again. The Esquimaux did not go off this day
but will leave with the first fair wind. Ther: by almost

lines.transcription: Monday 8th Wind West & S.W. a Beautiful mild day. men
employed, thus, W. Oman With four Esquimaux went
down to the old Fort with one of the Blubber Boats
8 took up the Cargo of the Grow. that drove on
there yesterday, & got Broken or almost Split in
two - Summer & Buck assisting Mr Hack Came
in the Trading shop to Settle with the Esquys
the other men with 3 Indians loading the John
Martin & got all the Cargo on Board except to
Hand Sledges & deers Homes - The Result of trade
from 24 Whale Hunters and 10 others that arrived
this morning is as follows Vizr 125 Whales 12Z.
White foxes 1 Cross & 3 Blue F. 12 prime & 5 Stage
wolves 2 wolverance 4Z0 Rein deer patch & 14 pairs
of Boats, - Some Sonaws Fine with a few trifle - I have
again for their return to salmon to River white fish from the N

on my arrival here I found that Dunning had Died
30th August and that William Oman was 10 Sick for
a long time afterwards that he was unable to Do any
work or to take care of the Place; So that I amue
Grey had to take charge and I must lay that he
had done his Bests and got all the work Fine that
Mr Anderson ordered, he also got the tents & Canoe
that was Sent to the Cross By W's Anderson, - all
the Churchill Crees arrived at York & 24 Sept 18
except Charlie that Died at Goose Lake, - I think
there must have been some foul-play there

paragraphs.llm_text: Saturday 7th Wind. S.E. moderate and cloudy all day. Oman & son, with Andrew, arrived from the Bushy Islands with 30 Partridges, 10 each for their week's hunt, poor hunting. Adam & Oulibuck also were hunting; Adam killed 6 and outibuck 4 Partridges - they say the Partridges are plentiful but wild; all the other men continue at their former employment. There is 28 to 31 above zero; the weather is so warm that we cannot go on with wood-hauling so that we shall be out of wood & Provisions at the same time one week more will run us ashore if the weather continues mild; the River is again open abreast of the Bushy Islands and as far as can be seen above and below.

paragraphs.llm_text: Tuesday 1st Wind North Blowing a gale with Snow and drifting. The Indians Started this morning on their return, 2 3/4 lbs in Furs; the Result of the meat trade will appear hereafter, it is the most miserable trade that has ever been here. I wish now that I had sent the men to the South Lake when I intended. I tried to get one of the Indians to guide our men to Knife Lake But none of them would consent on account of their families, as this is a very hard season with them. - Sam's Grey & Bungie Bros. paragraphs.llm_text: Friday 26th Wind West: a beautiful, day, The: 2nd & above Zero: Adam on the Sick List with a sore hand that the dog bit yesterday, Oman brought home 2 loads of wood & S.W., &c. - no alteration in the employment of the others; 5 Chipewyans Home guards arrived this afternoon they are from 8 others that they left at their tents having nothing to come with; their report is like their hunts most miserable, and complain much of sickness and want of deer last summer - the results of trade will appear hereafter, The mildness of the season have stopped them until this date owing to Seal River not being frozen, They were detained 5 nights at it.

lines.transcription: Ther: 15th Title: Zero: Oulighuck & Adam arrived last night
having only Killed 1 deer and left it at goose Lake
& started them off this morning with a Sledge each
to bring it home, - the Jazzy divlo thought to get,
r train of dogs to go galling about with and make
a two days trip with them laying on the Sleose, the
ogs has got enough to do to haul wood for them &
their families, as long as the Revisions lasts which
will not be long owing to their neglect Last Rum:
& extended to Send them both towards churchile
creek to try for deer but they were to long in the
and I changed my mind as it would have been
dark before they got half, way at their Rate of
walking __ Gibeault brot: home 2 loads of freems
preys leg healed up at, last ye Much against his wife
I am sure, & No alteration in the employment,
of the others except, young Oman that, I have
to take in place of Mary Grey for water as
The has got quite careless and will not attend,
to any thing about the Room she has also told
me lies to hide her faults,

lines.transcription: Monday 21st Wind S.V.E. moderate with a little snow
Palling, Ther 10 Sebs: to 9deg above Zero: Grey boots home 3 loads
wood, Summer & Oman cutting Ice, - I took a turn to
day, The deer appear to be plentiful, there has a
and of 10 Passed other side the mile Stone I followe
their tracks to Buttons Bay, and found they had crossing
& then went up to the Indian track, and crossed
other side the far point of Rocks, unto the winter
tack, when I again came to deer tracks which I
followed up to the upper end of the Rocks but did
not see them, those deer have passed either yesterday
or this morning, I also saw a good many postridged
tracks, I was extended to see Goose Lake, but it began
to snow and I turned for home, -
